name: Eremostachys laciniata
short: Very limited: 90 patients having hysterectomy had the same complication rate with placebo as with an extract-containing medicine (suppository in one group). Skin ointment trial: no adverse event data.
text: In a study of 90 patients having a hysterectomy (the abstract says they were randomly selected and divided into three groups of 30), one group received placebo and two received a medicine containing Eremostachys laciniata extract, in one of them as a suppository from 24 hours before to 24 hours after surgery; the rate of complications after surgery was the same in all three groups, and the authors concluded that the extract can be used without any significant side effects. A single-blinded trial of the rhizome extract as an ointment applied to the skin, compared with piroxicam ointment for 14 days in inflammatory joint conditions, concluded it was safe for topical use, but the abstract does not report any adverse event data. The human evidence is small and short-term. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
